n_blocks.description: How many blocks are on this page, counting every paragraph of body text, every heading and every table. A bulleted list is ONE block, however many bullets it has. You must output exactly this many blocks below.
n_blocks.title: N Blocks

table_column_counts.description: The column count of each REAL table, in order. A real table has a repeating grid: several rows sharing the same column positions. Text that is merely spaced out, or a single strip of label/value pairs, is NOT a table -- leave it out. Example: [6]. Use [] if there are no tables.
table_column_counts.title: Table Column Counts

has_header.description: True if the table's first row is a header of column LABELS (names describing the columns). False if the first row is already data -- for example a plain grid of numbers with no labels. When false, leave header empty and put every row in rows.
has_header.title: Has Header

n_data_rows.description: How many entries the rows list below will contain. Count EVERY row you are about to output, including full-width divider rows and section-heading rows. Exclude only the header row.
n_data_rows.title: N Data Rows

header.description: The header row as a list of column labels. Use [] when has_header is false.
header.title: Header

rows.description: The data rows, each a list of cell strings. Every row must have exactly n_cols entries -- pad with empty strings "" where a cell is blank or merged. Copy cell text exactly as printed, including $ , % and + - signs.
rows.title: Rows

kind.description: What structural kind of non-table block this is.
kind.title: Kind

text.description: Full text of the block, exactly as printed. Use REAL line breaks for lines that are separate on the page, such as the lines of an address. Never write the two characters backslash-n.
text.title: Text

align.description: How this block sits horizontally on the page: 'center' if it is centred across the page, 'right' if it is pushed to the right margin, otherwise 'left'.
align.title: Align

size.description: Size of this block's text compared with the page's ordinary body text. Use 'normal' for ordinary body text -- most blocks on most pages are normal. Use 'large' ONLY for titles and letterheads that are visibly bigger than the body, and 'small' ONLY for footers, footnotes and fine print that are visibly smaller.
size.title: Size

bold.description: True if this block is printed in bold or heavy type.
bold.title: Bold

analysis.description: Your reasoning about the page layout, BEFORE extracting.

blocks.description: Every block on the page, in top-to-bottom reading order.
blocks.title: Blocks
